sources.entry: mongoengine - A Python object-document mapper for working with MongoDB.

summary.one_liner: MongoEngine is a Python object-document mapper (ORM-like layer on top of PyMongo) for working with MongoDB.
summary.what_it_does: MongoEngine lets you define document classes in Python with typed fields such as StringField, DateTimeField and ListField, then save, query and count them in MongoDB. It supports inheritance between document classes, so a query on a superclass returns instances of its subclasses. Querying uses a objects-style interface, for example filtering by tags or counting documents per subtype. The README names optional extras for a flexible date parser (python-dateutil), image fields (Pillow), and signals (blinker). Documentation is hosted on Read the Docs and includes a tutorial, user guide and API reference.
use_cases: define MongoDB document schemas in Python
query MongoDB collections with Python objects
store blog posts or similar documents with subtypes in MongoDB
replace raw PyMongo calls with a higher-level mapper
validate document fields before saving to MongoDB
store image files in MongoDB with ImageField
how_to_run: python -m pip install .  (from a source checkout)
python -m pip install -e ".[test]"  (for development and tests)
pytest tests/  (requires MongoDB running on the standard port)
tox  (runs tests across supported Python and PyMongo versions)
notable: ORM-like document mapping on top of PyMongo with typed fields
Inheritance support: querying a base class returns subclass instances
Tested against MongoDB v4.4 through v8.0
Official docs on Read the Docs with tutorial, user guide and API reference
Optional extras for dates, images and signals
caveats: The mongoengine.org domain is no longer controlled by the project and appears to be an expired domain takeover; use the GitHub and Read the Docs links instead
Future MongoDB versions are supported in principle but not actively tested
Requires Python 3.10 or newer and a running MongoDB for tests
